title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page, numbered 166, of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie', Grothendieck), §§12.8–13.1. It appears as an insertion among the 1975–76 manuscript notes on divided-power De Rham complexes; the neighbouring pages are unrelated.

Setting of §12. S is a henselian trait and X → S is a proper flat curve. The generic fibre is smooth, and the special fibre X_0 is reduced with only ordinary double points x_λ (λ ∈ L). J is the Jacobian of the generic fibre; it has semistable reduction. M is the character group of the toric part of the special fibre of the Néron model of J; its rank equals the first Betti number of the dual graph of X_0. For each double point x_λ, φ_{x_λ} : M → Z is the linear form attached to that point, essentially the edge coordinate in the cycle space of the dual graph.

Theorem 12.5 is the Picard–Lefschetz formula for curves. When X is regular, the monodromy pairing on M equals Σ_λ φ_{x_λ} ⊗ φ_{x_λ}. Its proof in 12.8 reduces, by deformation and specialization, to a situation X^λ over S^λ, where S^λ is a trait of characteristic zero. The first line of this page concludes that reduction.

Remark 12.9. The reduction also brings one to the classical Picard–Lefschetz case: X_0 has a single singular point. Then X_0 has one or two irreducible components. With one component the node is non-separating and rank M = 1. With two components the node is separating and rank M = 0; the toric part vanishes, so the Jacobian of the generic fibre has good reduction.

12.10. Without assuming X regular, the local equation at x_λ is xy = π^{d_λ}, with d_λ ≥ 1 as in (12.8.12). The same proof then gives monodromy pairing u = Σ_λ d_λ φ_{x_λ} ⊗ φ_{x_λ} : M ⊗ M → Z. This is the dual-graph / edge-length description of the monodromy pairing, equivalently the Grothendieck–Raynaud pairing.

§13 begins the comparison with the transcendental, complex-analytic theory. 13.1 recalls commutative analytic group spaces A over an analytic space S.
errors: No mathematical errors. The remark is correct: one node with two components means a separating node, so rank M = 0 and the Jacobian has abelian (good) reduction; one component means a non-separating node and rank M = 1.
Typos in the typescript: 'monodormie' for 'monodromie'; 'correspondants' should be 'correspondant'.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript page of published SGA 7 Exposé IX, slipped into the archive folder. Everything on it is in print and credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: 'monodormie' is the typescript's own typo for 'monodromie', faithfully transcribed.
'484' appears twice: once as a handwritten pencil number and once as an archive stamp. The handwritten '102' at bottom left is the folio number within cote 136.
